description: Cross-period certification. Phases 1-8 each certify one cutoff. The engine withholds every semi-monthly cutoff independently from a table, so the only mechanism that corrects a whole year (mid-year hire, mid-year raise, 13th-month pool, bracket boundaries) is the year-end annualization. Phase 4 takes its output as an approved input and never recomputes it. Part A runs the real annualize() on hand-derived cases. Part B runs the real payroll engine for all 24 cutoffs of 2026 for four employees, then the real runYearEndAnnualization over the released year. Every expected value is hand-derived below from the published rules, never copied from engine output.

sources.thirteenthMonthAndBenefits: NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7)(e) as amended by TRAIN: 13th-month pay and other benefits are exempt up to a combined 90,000; the excess is taxable compensation. PD 851 / DOLE: 13th-month pay is one twelfth of the basic salary actually earned in the calendar year.
sources.contributions: SSS employee 5% of the monthly salary credit (cap 35,000, so at most 1,750 per month); PhilHealth employee 2.5% of monthly basic salary (floor 10,000, cap 100,000); Pag-IBIG employee 2% of a fund salary capped at 10,000 (200 per month). With 'split' timing each cutoff carries half the monthly amount.

assumptions: Tax year 2026, 24 semi-monthly cutoffs (1-15 and 16-end of month), each paid on its last day. The employer uses 'split' statutory deduction timing, so every cutoff collects half the monthly contribution.

Monthly salaried employees with no attendance deductions, supplementary pay, loans, allowances or leave. Regular payroll runs do not pay 13th-month, so the entitlement is accrued by the annualization as unpaid 13th month and added to gross, exactly as year-end processing treats it.
Year-end annualization reads Released runs, so each calculated run is set to Released directly in the fixture. The release approval workflow itself is not exercised here.
Expected values for annualize() use tax = bracket base + rate x (taxable - floor), rounded to the centavo, then adjustment = tax due - tax withheld (positive = collect, negative = refund).

taxableAtExemptionLimit.description: Gross 300,000 less contributions 50,000 = taxable exactly 250,000, the top of the exempt bracket: tax 0.00, nothing withheld, balanced.

oneHundredPesosIntoFifteenPercentBracket.description: Taxable 250,100: 15% x 100 = 15.00. Nothing was withheld, so 15.00 is collected.

taxableAtFourHundredThousand.description: Taxable exactly 400,000: 15% x 150,000 = 22,500.00, which equals the next bracket's base, so the table is continuous. Withheld 22,500.00: balanced.

taxableAtEightHundredThousand.description: Taxable exactly 800,000: 22,500 + 20% x 400,000 = 102,500.00, equal to the next base. Withheld 100,000.00: collect 2,500.00.

thirteenthMonthAtNinetyThousandCap.description: Gross 600,000 includes a 90,000 13th month, fully exempt. Non-taxable 90,000 + contributions 30,000 = 120,000; taxable 480,000; tax 22,500 + 20% x 80,000 = 38,500.00.

thirteenthMonthAboveCapTaxedOnce.description: Gross 630,000 includes a 120,000 13th month (30,000 more than the previous case). Only 90,000 is exempt; the 30,000 excess stays in gross and is taxed once: non-taxable 120,000; taxable 510,000; tax 22,500 + 20% x 110,000 = 44,500.00, which is 6,000.00 (20% of 30,000) above the previous case.

thirteenthMonthSharesPoolWithOtherBenefi.description: 13th month 60,000 + other benefits 40,000 share ONE 90,000 pool: pool 100,000, exempt 90,000, taxable excess 10,000. Gross 610,000; non-taxable 90,000 + 30,000 = 120,000; taxable 490,000; tax 22,500 + 20% x 90,000 = 40,500.00.

deMinimisExcessJoinsPool.description: 13th month 85,000 + de minimis excess 10,000 = pool 95,000: exempt 90,000, taxable 5,000. De minimis within ceilings 20,000 is fully exempt. Gross 700,000; non-taxable 90,000 + 20,000 + contributions 40,000 = 150,000; taxable 550,000; tax 22,500 + 20% x 150,000 = 52,500.00.

overWithheldEmployeeIsRefunded.description: Gross 360,000 incl. 30,000 13th month, contributions 29,400: non-taxable 59,400; taxable 300,600; tax 15% x 50,600 = 7,590.00. Withheld 12,088.80: refund 4,498.80.

contributionsLargerThanGrossFloorAtZero.description: Contributions exceed gross: taxable income floors at 0.00 and tax is 0.00; the 1,000.00 withheld is refunded.

minimumWageEarnerOnlyTaxedOnSupplementar.description: MWE: statutory wage is exempt, so taxable = taxable supplementary pay 20,000 + taxable benefit-pool excess 0 - contributions 10,000 = 10,000: tax 0.00.

minimumWageEarnerBenefitPoolExcessIsTaxa.description: MWE with a 100,000 13th month: 10,000 above the 90,000 pool is taxable. Taxable = supplementary 300,000 + pool excess 10,000 - contributions 20,000 = 290,000; tax 15% x 40,000 = 6,000.00; nothing was withheld from an MWE: collect 6,000.00.

fullYear.description: One organization, 24 cutoffs of 2026, four monthly employees. Every cutoff of an employee must match its segment exactly; the year-end row must match the annual literals.

steadyThirty.description: PHP 30,000/month all year. Cutoff gross 15,000; SSS 750.00, PhilHealth 375.00, Pag-IBIG 100.00; taxable 13,775.00; withholding 15% x (13,775 - 10,417) = 503.70 (matches Phase 2A EMP-006). Year: contributions (1,500 + 750 + 200) x 12 = 29,400; withheld 503.70 x 24 = 12,088.80. Annualization: gross 360,000 + unpaid 13th month 30,000 = 390,000; non-taxable 30,000 + 29,400 = 59,400; taxable 330,600; tax 15% x 80,600 = 12,090.00; collect 1.20 (the per-cutoff table differs from the annual table by rounding).

midYearHire.description: Hired 2026-07-01 at PHP 30,000/month: cutoffs 13-24 only, each identical to steadyThirty (503.70 withheld). Year: contributions 1,225 x 12 = 14,700; withheld 503.70 x 12 = 6,044.40. Annualization: gross 180,000 + unpaid 13th month (basic earned 180,000 / 12 = 15,000) = 195,000; non-taxable 15,000 + 14,700 = 29,700; taxable 165,300, below 250,000, so tax due 0.00 and the whole 6,044.40 withheld is refunded.

midYearRaise.description: PHP 20,000/month for cutoffs 1-12, PHP 40,000/month for cutoffs 13-24. First half: gross 10,000; SSS 500.00, PhilHealth 250.00, Pag-IBIG 100.00; taxable 9,150.00 (below 10,417): withholding 0.00 (Phase 2A EMP-001). Second half: gross 20,000; SSS MSC 35,000 cap -> 875.00; PhilHealth 2.5% x 40,000 = 1,000/month -> 500.00; Pag-IBIG 100.00; taxable 20,000 - 1,475 = 18,525.00; withholding 937.50 + 20% x (18,525 - 16,667) = 1,309.10. Year: contributions (850 x 12) + (1,475 x 12) = 10,200 + 17,700 = 27,900; withheld 1,309.10 x 12 = 15,709.20. The 13th month uses basic ACTUALLY earned, 120,000 + 240,000 = 360,000 / 12 = 30,000, not 12 x the final salary. Annualization: gross 360,000 + 30,000 = 390,000; non-taxable 30,000 + 27,900 = 57,900; taxable 332,100; tax 15% x 82,100 = 12,315.00; refund 3,394.20 because the semi-monthly table over-withholds on the higher half-year pay.

limitations: Regular payroll runs do not pay 13th month, so the year-end 13th month is the accrued entitlement added at annualization; a 13th month actually paid inside a cutoff (and the December cutoff binding of the adjustment) is not exercised here.
All four employees are monthly salaried with no attendance, supplementary pay, loans or allowances; daily/hourly workers (Phase 8) and attendance pay (Phase 5) are not run across a year.
Imported prior-provider history, prior-employer evidence and numbered-2316 reconciliation are separate flows and are not covered.
Release approval is bypassed: runs are set to Released in the fixture, so approval gating is not exercised.
No practitioner has reviewed the expected values; they are derived from the cited rules and need a qualified Philippine payroll/tax review before being relied on for filing.
